The lifecycle gap is in [poll.go](/app/internal/storage/fs/poll.go:12): `Poll` receives its context and update callback at launch, but `Poller` retains neither a cancellation function nor a way to wait for the goroutine. It also does not stop its ticker.

All five backends launch a poller without retaining it: [Git](/app/internal/storage/fs/git/store.go:126), [local](/app/internal/storage/fs/local/store.go:43), [S3](/app/internal/storage/fs/object/s3/store.go:79), [Azure Blob](/app/internal/storage/fs/object/azblob/store.go:69), and [OCI](/app/internal/storage/fs/oci/store.go:56). Their `SnapshotStore` types have no `Close()` method. The likely fix is to give `Poller` a stored `UpdateFunc`, internal cancellable context, and completion signal; each backend should retain its poller and have `Close()` cancel and wait for it. Git’s fixed-hash path starts no poller, so `Close()` must be safe there too.

Existing tests use context cancellation during cleanup but do not establish that `Close()` waits for an active update. A further uncertainty is that the Git, local, S3, and Azure update methods currently ignore their context, so shutdown may have to wait for an in-flight update to finish. I did not edit source or tests; this run was scoped to fault localization.

Implemented polling lifecycle management across Git, local, S3, Azure Blob, and OCI snapshot stores. Each store now retains its poller and exposes `Close()`, which safely returns when no polling is active. The poller cancels its context, stops its ticker, and waits for an active update to finish.

Added lifecycle tests. The full `internal/storage/fs/...` suite and focused race tests passed with `GOPROXY=off`.

VERDICT: FIX

The patch leaves two shutdown gaps:

- [Poller.Close()](/app/internal/storage/fs/poll.go:103) can return before a newly launched `Poll()` goroutine starts. Register the goroutine before launch and wait for its completion on every close path.
- The application factory returns an [fs.Store wrapper](/app/internal/storage/fs/store.go:35) that does not expose the backend’s `Close()`. Forward `Close()` through the wrapper so callers can stop polling.
